summary: NHTSA rejected AMC's discrimination argument, stating that the flexibility gained by manufacturers including captive imports with high fuel economy is no greater than the flexibility enjoyed by a manufacturer that domestically produces high-fuel-economy nonpassenger automobiles.
text:
As to AMC's discrimination argument, it should be noted that while the inclusion of the imports may give a manufacturer

importing nonpassenger automobiles with high fuel economy some added flexibility in achieving the standard, this flexibility is no greater than the flexibility that would be enjoyed by a manufacturer which domestically manufactures a number of nonpassenger automobiles with high fuel economy.
